column1: # label-rules.tsv — deterministic sender/subject -> Gmail label rules.
# Normally GENERATED/CURATED from the user's real inbox by the
# `label-rules-curator` agent. Run scripts/discover-senders.sh first to see the
# common "email pathways" (top sender domains + subject words), then edit the
# rows below. This file is plain data: no code and no LLM at run time.
# Format: TAB-separated, one rule per line, three columns:
#   <label> <TAB> <from-domains> <TAB> <subject-terms>
#   * label         : Gmail label to apply. Created automatically by
#                     scripts/nightly-label.sh if it does not already exist.
#   * from-domains  : space-separated bare domains, e.g. "chase.com amex.com".
#                     Use a single "-" when the rule is subject-only.
#   * subject-terms : a raw Gmail subject expression, already OR-joined and
#                     quoted where needed, e.g.  "final notice" OR overdue
#                     Leave empty (or omit) for sender-only rules.
#   * Lines starting with "#" and blank lines are ignored.
#   * Domains/terms within a rule are OR-ed. When both a from-domain and subject
#     terms are present the rule matches sender AND subject.
# The taxonomy below is a curated DEFAULT with illustrative example senders.
# Replace the senders with the ones you actually receive before trusting it.
